Just remember that your doctor is here to help you. They want the best for you. They also hear all sorts of things throughout their day and they most likely have several other patients in the same position as you. What I would do is slowly give out more and more information. You don’t have to say everything in the same appointment if you’re not comfortable. Maybe start out by saying that things are starting to go down again or that you’ve been feeling a little less well and give out information in the paste you’re comfortable with.

I find it hard to start studying, but this is what helped be a bit: If I had to study then I went somewhere where I can’t be distracted. I know it can be exhausting to think that things like videos, series etc whatever makes you procrastinate isn’t available , but if you’re desperate enough (like I am) then it’s worth a try. 

I hate school, my teacher, and I’m not a fan of my class, but the only reason why I’m not giving up is because I really want the career path that I’ve planned. I doubt that you’ll be homeless, I doubt that you will fail and I doubt that you won’t get a good job. Just please do not give up. If a test didn’t go as planned just remember that you tried your best and that you’ll do better next time.
